content: I’ll trace depfile loading, dyndep edge insertion, and dirty-state propagation, then add a focused regression test before running the relevant test suite.

The evidence points to traversal-order invalidation: `copy`’s depfile visits `other` as a leaf before scanning the order-only `stamp`; loading `stamp.dd` later assigns `other` to the dirty `stamp` edge, but the already-visited depfile input is not reconsidered. I’m checking the graph-mutation API and nearest test fixture only, to patch the invalidation at the correct boundary.

Acceptance criteria are now concrete: input traversal must finish (including dyndep graph mutations) before an edge derives dirtiness from any non-order-only input; the existing input order, order-only semantics, mtimes, and diagnostics must remain unchanged. I’ll implement that post-order evaluation and add the minimal in-memory regression.
The transaction failed on a stale test anchor, so no files changed. I’m refreshing only the two intended hunks and will reapply the same focused fix against current context.

The second patch attempt was also rejected without mutation because the writer requires a complete read before replacing that loop. I’m satisfying that snapshot requirement; the implementation/test design remains unchanged.

The patch gate still does not recognize the paginated read as complete. I’ll read the remaining explicit line range and then use a fully contextual hunk, avoiding any ambiguity in the writer’s deletion check.

The safety check is classifying the unnumbered patch format as a context-free deletion despite surrounding context. I’ll submit the same narrow change as a numbered unified diff; no repository mutation has occurred yet.
